thread:
maria-support: Hi team — escalating a repro for customer Skyline (tenant id: tenant-348). They see intermittent auth failures + token refresh latency spikes around 2026-03-14T18:12Z. Main request IDs: req-7a1b2c, req-7a1b2d, req-7a1b3f. Can someone help with a minimal repro bundle (pod logs, node logs, gpu metrics) and a curl snippet to reproduce?

kai-sre: Thanks — can you confirm the affected region and the dedicated pool name? Also need the failing pod names or label selector.

maria-support: Region eu-west-1, dedicated pool: reserved-eu-prod-3. Pod labels: app=inference, tenant=tenant-348. Example pod seen in traces: inference-rc-5f7b9.

kai-sre: OK. Steps I need from the on-call or the customer:
- kubectl logs for the pod(s) for the 18:00-18:20 window (include stderr).
- kubectl describe pod \u003cpod-name\u003e and kube-events for that timeframe.
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-03-14 18:00" --until "2026-03-14 18:25" on the node.
- dmesg + /var/log/messages around the time of the spike.
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,fan.speed --format=csv -l 1 for 2m (or sailor snapshot).
- dcgm-exporter / prometheus scrape for GPU memory/throughput if available.

kai-sre: Also run a request-level capture: export a short curl that includes X-Request-ID so we can match server logs. Example below. Please redact tokens before uploading.

devon-eng: Here's a minimal curl we use for repros (mask token):
```
curl -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req-REPRO-0001" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"echo hi","max_tokens":8}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/infer
```

devon-eng: If you hit the auth error, capture the full response headers and save the raw response (curl -D - --output body.txt).

acme-ops: We tried to reproduce. Attached sample outputs: pod log tail (snippet):
"2026-03-14T18:12:03Z ERROR auth middleware token refresh failed for tenant-348 req=7a1b2c ttl=0"
"2026-03-14T18:12:03Z WARN kv-cache miss for prefix xyz req=7a1b2c"

acme-ops: GPU metric snapshot we pulled with nvidia-smi at 18:12:10: GPU-Util 98%, memory.used 14234MiB, temp 78C. Two minutes later at 18:14:10 GPU-Util dropped to 3% and requests queued up.

kai-sre: That pattern (spike then drop) looks like a worker restart or throttling. Please run on the node:
```
ps aux | grep inference
systemctl status containerd --no-pager
cat /var/log/kern.log | grep -i oom
```
Also attach kubelet logs as requested.

maria-support: I started a support bundle upload for the customer via obs-bot. acme-ops — when you have the files (pod logs, node journal, nvidia-smi csv, kube-events), upload to the pre-signed URL and post the path here. Make sure to replace any live tokens with REDACTED.

obs-bot: Support bundle created: s3://redwood-support-bundles/tenant-348/1712349999-skyline-repro.tar.gz (expires in 72h). Please confirm upload.

acme-ops: Uploaded -> s3://redwood-support-bundles/tenant-348/1712349999-skyline-repro.tar.gz. Included files: pod-logs.txt, kube-events.json, node-journal.log, nvidia-smi.csv, curl-response-body.txt, auth-error-headers.txt.

kai-sre: Thanks. I'll pull the bundle and start a quick grep across logs for X-Request-IDs and auth subsystem traces. Next steps: if we see token store latency, we may ask for a quick pcap of control-plane calls or a kvstore latency trace.

devon-eng: If we need a quick repro on our side, I might ask for a small pod-level docker image that runs the same client and token refresh sequence; otherwise the curl with X-Request-ID + sample token (REDACTED) should be enough.

maria-support: Great — leaving this with kai for triage. I'll update the customer ticket with the bundle link and the curl snippet. acme-ops, thanks for the fast turnaround :thumbsup:

kai-sre: Ping me if you see any node-level OOMs or driver resets in the bundle, I'll coordinate with infra for live investigation.

acme-ops: Noted — we'll stand by for any follow-ups.
